access.edition_or_version: Meditations: with Selected Correspondence, trans. Robin Hard, intro. Christopher Gill (Oxford World's Classics, 2011)

mechanics.premise: Practical Stoic exercises: reminding oneself of principle under the pressure of daily life and mortality.
mechanics.argumentative_stance: Self-addressed admonition that abstracts a concrete occasion into a general rule about conduct and impermanence.
mechanics.point_of_view: Second-person or impersonal address to oneself (distanced self-address), not narrative recollection.
mechanics.structure: Short, unconnected entries grouped only by recurring themes; no plot or linear argument.
mechanics.style_and_devices: Compressed maxim, antithesis, repetition of key terms (nature, reason, mortality), analogy drawn from crafts and nature.
mechanics.imagery: Cosmic and surgical imagery: the view from above, the body as instrument, time as a river.
mechanics.emotional_progression: Agitation steadied into acceptance through repetition of principle.
mechanics.critical_reception: Central text of Stoicism and of contemplative prose; studied as a model of philosophical self-address.
mechanics.failure_or_misuse_signals: Maxim without situation becomes abstract moralising; second-person address without a concrete trigger reads as sermon.
